words.definition: A group of countries or regions ruled by one power.

contextSentences.en: The Byzantine Empire survived the fall of the Western Roman Empire by almost a thousand years.
The Mongol Empire in the 13th century was the largest contiguous land empire in history.

words.example_en: This experiment shows how empire works.
words.example_sk: Tento experiment ukazuje, ako funguje ríša.

words.definition: A sequence of rulers from the same family.

contextSentences.en: The Ming Dynasty ruled China from 1368 to 1644 and is known for completing the Great Wall.
Dynastic marriages were used in the Middle Ages to forge political alliances between kingdoms.

words.definition: A major change in political or social systems.

contextSentences.en: The American Revolution of 1776 led to independence from British colonial rule.
The October Revolution of 1917 ended tsarist rule in Russia and led to the founding of the Soviet Union.

words.example_en: We studied the concept of revolution yesterday.

words.definition: An advanced human society with culture and institutions.

contextSentences.en: The Mesopotamian civilisation between the Euphrates and Tigris is considered the cradle of writing.
Key features of a civilisation include writing, cities, specialised labour, and organised government.

words.example_en: The teacher explained the term civilisation.

words.definition: A king, queen, or other hereditary ruler.

contextSentences.en: Queen Victoria was the longest-reigning monarch of the 19th century.
Louis XIV of France embodied absolute monarchy with his famous saying "I am the state".

words.example_en: We studied the concept of monarch yesterday.

words.definition: A formal agreement between states or nations.

contextSentences.en: The Peace of Westphalia in 1648 ended the Thirty Years' War through a comprehensive treaty.
The Treaty of Maastricht in 1992 laid the foundations for today's European Union.

words.definition: A fight between armies or military forces.

contextSentences.en: The Battle of Stalingrad is widely regarded as the turning point of the Second World War.
At the naval Battle of Salamis in 480 BC, a smaller Greek fleet defeated a much larger Persian one.

words.example_en: This experiment shows how battle works.
words.example_sk: Tento experiment ukazuje, ako funguje bitka.

words.definition: A territory controlled by a more powerful country.

contextSentences.en: Most African countries gained independence from their colonial rulers during the 1950s and 1960s.
The economic exploitation of a colony by its ruling power was a defining feature of colonialism.

words.example_en: This experiment shows how colony works.
words.example_sk: Tento experiment ukazuje, ako funguje kolónia.

words.definition: The study of human history through remains and artefacts.

contextSentences.en: Excavations at Pompeii have given archaeology a detailed picture of everyday Roman life.
Modern archaeology uses non-invasive techniques such as ground-penetrating radar to explore sites.

words.example_en: The archaeology is important in this field.
words.example_sk: Archeológia je v tejto oblasti dôležitý.

words.definition: An object made by humans in the past.

contextSentences.en: The bust of Nefertiti is one of the most famous ancient Egyptian artifacts and is housed in Berlin.
Each artifact tells a story and provides clues about the society in which it was created.

words.example_en: We studied the concept of artifact yesterday.

words.definition: The arrangement of events in the order they happened.

contextSentences.en: Radiocarbon dating allows scientists to establish a precise chronology for organic prehistoric finds.
The chronology of the Egyptian pharaohs was reconstructed using hieroglyphic texts.

words.definition: The traditions, monuments, and values passed down from the past.

contextSentences.en: The ancient heritage of Greece lives on today in science, philosophy, and democratic ideals.
UNESCO works worldwide to protect the cultural and natural heritage of humanity.

words.example_en: The teacher explained the term heritage.

contextSentences.en: The medieval feudal system governed land ownership and obligations between lords and vassals.
Medieval plague epidemics killed an estimated one-third of the European population in the 14th century.

words.example_en: The medieval is important in this field.
words.example_sk: Stredoveký je v tejto oblasti dôležitý.

words.definition: Belonging to a very distant past.

contextSentences.en: Ancient city-states such as Athens and Sparta shaped the political ideas of Western civilisation.
Ancient Rome developed a sophisticated legal system that forms the basis of many modern legal codes.

words.example_en: The teacher explained the term ancient.

words.definition: The movement of people from one region to another.

contextSentences.en: The migration of people from rural areas to cities shaped European history in the 19th century.
Historians estimate that the migration from Europe to the Americas in the 19th century involved millions of people.
